workingTitle: An independent reconstruction confirms M87*'s black hole ring
publicationStatus: Peer-reviewed open-access Nature article published November 11, 2026
coreFacts: An independent method reconstructed a compact ring from public Event Horizon Telescope datasets spanning 2017, 2018 and 2021.
The method uses closure invariants formed from telescope triplets, which preserve source morphology while cancelling station-based calibration errors.
The mean ring diameter is 42.2 plus or minus 1.5 microarcseconds.
Using nominal scaling parameters, the diameter implies a black hole mass of 6.5 plus or minus 0.5 billion solar masses.
Ring width, central brightness and some fine-scale features remain sensitive to the reconstruction method.
sourceStatus: Full peer-reviewed paper, data and code statements, license, and authors' institution release read; numerical claims and limitations checked.
caveats: The result reanalyses existing EHT observations rather than collecting a new black hole image.
The mass inference depends on the adopted distance and theoretical ring-size scaling.
Ring width and brightness asymmetry are less robust than the ring's diameter and overall morphology.
